title: Artifact reference
description: A reference to one file a run produced. The SDK returns references, never bare file paths: a reference carries the file's content hash and type, so it stays meaningful away from the machine that wrote it and its bytes can be verified after download.

name.description: The artifact's name, unique within its run, for example `run_spec.json`, `run_info.json` or `log_info.json`, or a per-capture product named `<base>-t<task>-c<capture>.img` (and `.img.hdr`) as the platform template writes it. It is the last segment of the `get_artifact` path.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the artifact's bytes, as 64 lowercase hex digits. The bytes returned by `get_artifact`, or read from `uri`, must hash to this value.

media_type.description: The media type of the bytes, for example `application/json` for a run spec or a log, `application/octet-stream` for an ENVI image and `text/plain` for its header.

uri.description: Where the bytes can be read: a `file://` URI when the run was executed locally, or a download URL when it was executed by a server.

frame.description: For an artifact that belongs to one capture of a multi-frame run (an image, its header, a truth product), the zero-based index of that capture, in task order. Absent for an artifact that belongs to the run as a whole (the run spec, the engine logs).

role.description: `built / internal` (`tests/test_artifact_roles.py`). What the artifact is to a user of the run, from a free vocabulary of lowercase words whose initial set is: `product` (the engine's output imagery or data), `truth` (truth images or annotations that describe a product), `preview` (an image for looking at, not measurement), `log` (what the engine or the worker reported while running), `config` (the inputs as executed: the resolved run spec, the engine's own configuration files) and `metadata` (descriptions of other artifacts: image headers, scene or orbit descriptions). A client treats a role it does not know as an opaque label. The engine's adapter assigns it, never a file name rule of the backend; the resolved run spec is `config`. Every reference a backend builds carries it; a reference stored before roles existed has none.
